Assert that a data frame is empty

Source: R/expect_empty.R
expect_empty.Rd

A pipeline-friendly validation checkpoint. Express a rule as "the set of violations must be empty", build that set with an ordinary filter(), and pipe it in. Emits a success alert when the data frame has zero rows, otherwise warns or aborts with the number of offending rows and a preview of the first few.

Usage

expect_empty(
  data,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = "The dataset is not empty.",
  abort_msg = NULL,
  log = getOption("daos.check_log"),
  dump = getOption("daos.check_dump")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble.

success_msg

Message shown (and logged) when data is empty. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the log names every check that ran, and "The dataset is empty." otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown (and logged) when data is not empty and no abort_msg is set. Default: "The dataset is not empty.".

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when data is not empty. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

log

Optional path to a log file. The directory is created automatically. Defaults to getOption("daos.check_log").

dump

Optional directory. When the check fails, the offending rows are written there as a timestamped CSV file (UTF-8 with BOM, so Excel reads æøå correctly). Defaults to getOption("daos.check_dump").

Value

data invisibly.

Details

Messages are shown literally: braces are not interpolated, so regular expressions such as "^\\d{8}$" are safe to use in a message.

A failed check signals a condition of class daos_check_failure (a warning or an error) that carries the offending rows in its violations field. Scheduled pipelines can catch it and keep the rows:

tryCatch(
  expect_empty(bad_rows, abort_msg = "Bad rows"),
  daos_check_failure = \(e) saveRDS(e$violations, "bad_rows.rds")
)

Logging and dumping

log appends one line per check to a text file, and dump writes the offending rows to a CSV file in a directory. Both default to a global option, so a script can switch them on once at the top instead of repeating the path in every check:

options(
  daos.check_log  = f("log/{nowf()}_checks.log"),
  daos.check_dump = "log/violations"
)

A log line has the form time | symbol | message | rows [| dump file]:

2026-06-11 09:00:03 | ✔ | Check passed: NA ids | 0 rows
2026-06-11 09:00:03 | ! | Negative amounts | 3 rows | log/violations/20260611_090003_Negative_amounts.csv

See also

expect_none() to check a condition without leaving the pipeline, expect_unique() for keys, tally_violations() to run many rules at once, and flag_duplicates().

Examples

# Success: no rows
data.frame() |> expect_empty()
#> ✔ The dataset is empty.

# Warning: unexpected rows
dplyr::filter(ggplot2::mpg, cyl > 6) |>
  expect_empty(warn_msg = "Eight-cylinder cars found")
#> Warning: Eight-cylinder cars found
#> ℹ 70 rows found:
#>   manufacturer = "audi", model = "a6 quattro", displ = 4.2, year = 2008, cyl =
#>   8, trans = "auto(s6)...
#>   manufacturer = "chevrolet", model = "c1500 suburban 2wd", displ = 5.3, year =
#>   2008, cyl = 8, tran...
#>   manufacturer = "chevrolet", model = "c1500 suburban 2wd", displ = 5.3, year =
#>   2008, cyl = 8, tran...
#>   manufacturer = "chevrolet", model = "c1500 suburban 2wd", displ = 5.3, year =
#>   2008, cyl = 8, tran...
#>   manufacturer = "chevrolet", model = "c1500 suburban 2wd", displ = 5.7, year =
#>   1999, cyl = 8, tran...
#>   ... and 65 more

# Abort: treat unexpected rows as a hard error
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dplyr::filter(dplyr::starwars, height < 0) |>
  expect_empty(abort_msg = "Impossible: negative height")
} # }

# With logging, set once for the whole script:
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
options(daos.check_log = f("log/{nowf()}/checks.log"))

dplyr::starwars |>
  dplyr::filter(name == "Harry Potter") |>
  expect_empty(warn_msg = "Harry Potter rows")
} # }
